notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
County school systems are part of county government in Tennessee, so school spending is included (it is left out of the services and overhead shares).
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Debt service leaves out $22,748,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the county did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Payments to other governments ($1,723,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Tennessee county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Tennessee yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Wilson County Sheriff's Office has access to SoundThinking's CrimeTracer (formerly Coplink X) investigative platform through a statewide contract announced in April 2021.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012348, citing PR News Wire

redFlags.unscoredReason: Not scored: every police department in the state has this through a statewide contract, so it is not a local decision.

redFlags.label: Predictive policing
redFlags.detail: The Wilson County Sheriff's Office has access to a predictive analytics system developed by IBM to identify locations where vehicle crashes and DUIs are likely to occur. All 95 county sheriffs in the state access the system, which is managed by the Tennessee Highway Patrol.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS007142, citing Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security
